high.title: After Several Consecutive Increases, Economists Hold Inflation and Selic Projections Steady; Focus Report for This Monday (29)
high.summary:
The latest BCB Focus Report (released Monday, June 29) shows that market consensus projections for both IPCA inflation and the Selic rate have stabilized after a series of consecutive upward revisions — a potentially significant signal that economists may be approaching a ceiling in their tightening expectations. For 2026, the IPCA forecast holds at 5.33%, meaningfully above the BCB's target band, reinforcing that inflation remains a key risk. The 2027 estimate nudged marginally higher to 4.17% (from 4.15%), while 2028 and 2029 projections remain anchored at 3.68% and 3.50%, respectively. The stabilization of Selic expectations — after multiple prior upward revisions — could suggest the market is pricing in a rate peak. **Key implications:** Bond traders should monitor whether this plateau in expectations translates into a rally at the short end of the yield curve. BRL could find modest support if the market perceives the BCB as being close to the end of its hiking cycle. Watch for next COPOM meeting guidance and whether incoming IPCA prints validate or challenge this apparent stabilization in the Focus survey.

medium.title: Real Return Treasury Bonds (Tesouro IPCA+) Near 10% and Weekly Market Highlights
medium.summary: The week was marked by the Brazilian Treasury (Tesouro Nacional) cancelling a scheduled bond auction amid significant stress in the government fixed income market, with market participants projecting yields on IPCA-linked bonds (Tesouro IPCA+) approaching the 10% real return threshold. This is a highly notable development for international bond investors, as a ~10% real yield on inflation-linked Brazilian sovereign paper signals either elevated fiscal risk premium, acute market illiquidity, or both. The cancellation of the auction itself is a bearish signal — the Treasury may have withdrawn to avoid locking in excessively high borrowing costs, suggesting the government is facing pressure in rolling over its debt. For BRL traders, persistently elevated real yields can be a double-edged sword: they may attract carry interest, but also reflect underlying fiscal credibility concerns that weigh on the currency. **Watch:** whether the Treasury reschedules the auction and at what clearing yield, as this will be a key gauge of market confidence in Brazil's fiscal trajectory.

medium.title: Middle Eastern Producers Maintain Oil and LNG Exports Despite Strait of Hormuz Attacks
medium.summary: Middle Eastern energy producers are continuing oil and LNG shipments through the Strait of Hormuz despite renewed vessel attacks and escalating US-Iran tensions, though shipping volumes have declined following strikes on a container ship (Thursday) and an oil tanker (Saturday). This geopolitical development carries indirect but meaningful relevance for Brazilian markets, particularly **Petrobras (PETR3/PETR4)**, which benefits from elevated global oil prices. Any sustained disruption to Hormuz shipping could push Brent crude higher, supporting Petrobras's revenue outlook and lending a positive impulse to the Ibovespa. Conversely, a sharp oil price spike also risks accelerating global inflation, complicating Banco Central do Brasil's inflation management and potentially impacting the BRL through risk-off sentiment. **Watch:** Brent crude price action and Petrobras shares at the open.

medium.title: Markets React to New US-Iran Ceasefire; Ibovespa in Dollar Terms Rises Today (29)
medium.summary: Global markets are trading predominantly higher on Monday following reports that the United States and Iran have agreed to halt retaliatory attacks, reopening the door to diplomatic negotiations. Over the weekend, the US carried out strikes against Iranian military targets in response to alleged Iranian involvement in attacks on the Strait of Hormuz — a development that had rattled commodity and risk markets. The de-escalation is providing broad risk-on sentiment across asset classes, with the Ibovespa rising in USD terms. For BRL and Brazilian equities, this is a constructive backdrop: lower geopolitical risk reduces commodity supply disruption fears and may ease oil price pressure, which is relevant for Brazil both as an oil producer (Petrobras) and as a country sensitive to global risk appetite. Fund managers should watch whether this ceasefire holds, as a re-escalation could quickly reverse the positive sentiment and pressure the BRL.

medium.title: Petrobras (PETR4) Receives R$170 Million in Second Installment of Diesel Subsidy Program
medium.summary: Petrobras (PETR4) disclosed receipt of R$170 million representing the second installment of the federal government's Economic Subsidy Program for diesel commercialization, covering the period of April 1–6. The program was created to mitigate the impact of rising oil prices stemming from the US-Iran conflict and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. While the individual payment amount is modest relative to Petrobras's scale, the subsidy mechanism carries fiscal policy relevance — government subsidies to Petrobras represent a contingent fiscal liability that fixed income and FX traders should monitor over time. Continued or expanding subsidy payments could add pressure to Brazil's fiscal accounts, which are a key driver of BRL and sovereign spread dynamics. Worth watching as oil price volatility persists.
